## Coast Live Oak Data Analysis

### Data Loading and Cleaning

```{r}
#loading packages to use in this project
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#reading in the soil moisture data 
Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

#reading in the SPAD data 
SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
```

Now to Clean! First, the soil moisture data

```{r}
Moist_Data_Raw #view the data so I remember what I need to do to clean it 

#First, I need to remove all of the excess NA values at the bottom 
Soil_Data <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  drop_na(Date) |> 
  #Now, I am only interested in the date, block, treatment, and VWC% readings (three per block)
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |> 
  #the VWC values are currently chr, and I need them in double format
  mutate(VWC1_perc= as.double(VWC1_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC2_perc = as.double(VWC2_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC3_perc = as.double(VWC3_perc)) |> 
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
  #Since I'm doing rain event, I want a before/after categorical variable
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-21" ~ "After"
  ))


#now that Ive done all of that, I also realized that I need one VWC per treatment/block combo (so each row)

Soil_Data <- Soil_Data |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(Soil_VWC = mean(c(VWC1_perc , VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE))
```

Next, the SPAD data

```{r}
SPAD_Data_Raw #viewing it so I can see what needs to be done 

#only include the rows for date, block, treatment, leaf 1-6, dead/alive
SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> 
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, Dead_Alive, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6, Notes) |> 
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
  #create column for Before/After rain event 
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-15" ~ "After"
  ))  |> 
  #filter out dead seedlings 
  filter(Dead_Alive == "Alive") |> 
  #now to create one SPAD reading for each sapling 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(mean_SPAD = mean(c(Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6), na.rm = TRUE))  
  #remove the two outlier SPAD values that were from brown leaves 


```

outliertest

```{r}
#filtering out the outlier values in SPAD_Data
#10 is just a random number that is more than the two outliers but less than the other values I wanted to keep 
 SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data |> 
  filter(mean_SPAD > 10)
```

### ANOVA

Testing the following relationship: SPAD \~ rain event \* habitat type

I want to test it with the interaction, as I expect the habitat type to have impacted how the rain water is received by the plant (the canopy/dead tree might keep it from getting as much rain, or might shield the soil from direct sunlight that would be causing evaporation).

In this section:

- Assumptions/ Normality tests

- ANOVA

- Figure

Assumptions Check

```{r}
#visualizing the data 
SPAD_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x=Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = Before_After)+
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{r}

# Build the linear model
SPAD_ANOVA_Model  <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment * Before_After, data = SPAD_Data)
#plot the model
plot(SPAD_ANOVA_Model, which = 2)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(SPAD_ANOVA_Model))

#run LAvene's test for homogeneity of variance 
plot(SPAD_ANOVA_Model, which = 1)

SPAD_Data |>  rstatix::levene_test(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment*Before_After)


```

Results of assumption check:

- Residuals of model look good

- P-value from Levene's test is .294 so it is not significant. Levene's test checks homogeneity of varience, and getting a number larger than 0.05 means we have homegeneity of variance. This means we have met out assumptions and can move on to the anova.

Let's do the ANOVA!

```{r}
anova(SPAD_ANOVA_Model)
summary(SPAD_ANOVA_Model)

#I also want to create an aov model that I will use later in my Tukey HSD 
SPAD_Model_aov <- aov(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment * Before_After, data = SPAD_Data)
summary(SPAD_Model_aov)

differentmodelaov <- aov(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment + Before_After, data = SPAD_Data)
```

The results we get tells us that while the combination between Treatment and Before_After is significant, Before_After on its own is VERY significant.

Now, which treatment/date combinations are statistically different?

```{r}
#Tukey HSD fo determine which pairs are different from each other 
TukeyHSD(SPAD_Model_aov)

```

The following treatment/date pairs were statistically significant:

AC before - AC after (p = 0.001), Ac before - NR after (p = 0.001), AC before - OS after (p = 0.007).

A few pairs were \~0.01 to 0.02 away from being statistically significant:

NR before - AC before (p = 0.069), AC before - DT after (p = 0.060)

None of the Treatment pairs (not being grouped by date) we significant.

Before-After on its own was very significant (p= 0.003)

So, my hypothesis that treatment and date were interacting is (mostly) rejectable, although it looks like the AC treatment before is significantly different from all of the after values. This isn't surprising, given that the NR, OS, and DT are similar in cover from sun and heat, while a living adult canopy would change the temperature and water in soil.

Now for the figure!

```{r}
SPAD_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x=Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = fct_rev(Before_After))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("Before"="skyblue", "After"="skyblue4")) +
  labs( y = "Leaf SPAD",
        x = "Microhabitat",
        title = "SPAD by Treatment and Rain Event",
        fill = "Relation to Rain Event") #labs is giving us labels on our graph 
```

This graph does a great job at showing how all of the means are similar, with the exception of the AC Before pair. However, after the results from the ANOVA, I'd also like a graph that is just before_after without treatment being considered.

```{r}
SPAD_Data |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x= fct_rev(Before_After), y = mean_SPAD, fill = fct_rev(Before_After)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("Before"="skyblue", "After"="skyblue4"))+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  labs( y = "Leaf SPAD",
        x = "Before/After Rain Event",
        title = "SPAD and Relation to Rain Event")
  
```

## Multivariate Regression

### 

Testing for the following relationship: SPAD \~ Soil Moisture and Habitat Type

In this section:

- Assumption/Normality tests

- Regression

- Figure

First, I need a data the SPAD data to have the soil moisture data

What I'm trying to tell R:

Create a new column in SPAD Data

In that column, place values from the Soil_VWC column in Soil_Data, based on rows with matching Block AND Treatment values

```{r}
#joinging SPAD_Data and Soil_Data, to get a frame that has Soil_Data for each row. Soil VWC values have one value for each block-treatment combo, so there will be repeats in the data frame 

SPAD_Soil_Data <- SPAD_Data  |> 
  left_join(Soil_Data, by = c("Block", "Treatment", "Before_After"), relationship = "many-to-many") |> 
  drop_na(Soil_VWC) #several NR treatments did not get soil VWC perc taken, resulting in a lot of NA values that I don't want to deal with. 


  
```

Assumptions/Normality Tests

```{r}
#Visualize the relationshiop 
SPAD_Soil_Data|> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x = Soil_VWC, y = mean_SPAD)+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

SPAD_Soil_Data|> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean_SPAD)+
  geom_boxplot()

SPAD_Soil_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x = Soil_VWC, y = mean_SPAD)+
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(vars(Treatment))
```

From the box plot, it does look like there may not be a significant difference between means of treatments, but in the third graph (the scatter plot) it seems there may be a relationship between means of spad with both temp and soil vwc.

```{r}
#create a linear model for the relationship
SPADSoillm <- lm(mean_SPAD~Soil_VWC * Treatment, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)

summary(SPADSoillm) #R2 = 0.2901

#this gave us a VERY low R2 value, so I'm going to create a few more linear models and see if those give us better results 

SPADSoillm2 <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Soil_VWC + Treatment, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)
SPADSoillm3 <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Soil_VWC, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)
SPADSoillm4 <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)

summary(SPADSoillm2) #R2 = 0.1372
summary(SPADSoillm3) #R2 = 0.095
summary(SPADSoillm4) #R2 = 0.03


AllTheThingslm<- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Soil_VWC * Before_After * Treatment, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)
summary(AllTheThingslm) #R2 is 0.38

SPADBFlm <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Before_After, data = SPAD_Soil_Data)
summary(SPADBFlm) #R2 is 0.116

#So, the lm that is looking at Soil VWC, rain event, AND treatment is the one that has the best line of best fit. However, for now I am going to just do the Soil plus treatment, then circle back to the everything model. 
```

```{r}

summary(SPADSoillm2)
coef(SPADSoillm2)["Soil_VWC"] * sd(SPAD_Soil_Data$Soil_VWC)/sd(SPAD_Soil_Data$mean_SPAD)

```

The important information here:

for mean_SPAD \~ Soil_VWC + Treatment

R2= 0.1372

p-value = 0.037

F = 2.704 (4, 68)

Beta coeff for Soil_VWC is -0.375. Because Treatment is a categorical variable, there is no Beta coeff for that.

Circling back to the everything model (SPAD as a response of soil vwc, treatment, and rain event)

```{r}

summary(AllTheThingslm)
```

The importnat information here:

- R2= 0.3805

- p-value = 0.00369

- F statistic= 2.788

I am, unfortunately, insane enough to try to graph this. So, plots and figure time!

```{r}
plot(AllTheThingslm, 2) #I just want the QQ plot 


```

```{r}
SPAD_Soil_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x = Soil_VWC, y = mean_SPAD, color = fct_rev(Before_After))+
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("Before"="skyblue", "After"="skyblue4"))+
  facet_wrap(vars(Treatment))+
  labs( y = "Leaf SPAD",
        x = "Soil Moisture Percent",
        title = "SPAD, Soil Moisture, Treatment, and Rain Event",
        color = "Relation to Rain Event")
```
